title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-evelyn-turner
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for redlining customer contracts (hosted API / dedicated / private). Quick notes for negotiation, clauses to flag, fallback language, and questions to escalate to outside counsel.

Top priorities / must-fix items:
- Liability cap: push for cap = greater of (fees paid in 12 mo OR $1M). watch carve-outs (IP infringement, gross negligence).
  - Ask: can we accept unlimited liability for data breach? No — try to narrow to willful misconduct only.
- Indemnity: limit to third-party claims arising from Customer use; carve out model output harms (customer use/ misuse).
- Data handling / ownership: company retains rights to service output? Prefer: customer owns their input & derived outputs; we retain right to use anonymized telemetry for ops/improvements unless customer opts out.
  - For regulated customers, add explicit non-use clause for model training and telemetry.
- Data residency & access: ensure data processed in agreed region (EU / US). For Private deployments, include KMS/HSM requirement and no-key-exfiltration clause.
- Security certifications: require SOC2 Type II + ISO27001 (if enterprise asks). Provide standard Attestation schedule (quarterly/annual).
- Audit & compliance: restrict audit rights to reasonable scope and frequency; use third-party SOC reports in lieu of customer on-site audits.
- Subprocessors / subcontracting: notify + right to object for sensitive sectors; include standard flowdown obligations.
- SLA & credits: define latency SLOs per endpoint (e.g., 95th percentile < X ms for n tokens). Credits limited to service fees; exclude downstream damages.
- Termination: notice period 30–60 days; termination for convenience by either party with 60 days notice; ensure post-termination data deletion timeline (30 days) and export assistance (10 days).
- Pricing & rate limits: include explicit rate limiting behavior and overage pricing; right to throttle for safety/abuse with notice.
- IP / outputs: customers claim ownership over prompts + outputs. We need a redline if customer asks for assignment of model IP.
- Model risk / harm disclaimers: include language that we do not guarantee accuracy of model outputs; customer is responsible for prod usage oversight.

Clauses to watch (language snippets):
- "as permitted by law" used in liability/injunctive relief sections — if overused, it can swallow protections.
- "Confidential information" definitions must include examples and exceptions (e.g., public domain, independently developed).
- Broad"purpose" language in license grants — prefer narrow "to use the service" scope.
- Data retention: watch for very long retention periods (default should be minimal, 90 days telemetry, 30 days backups).

Negotiation talking points (customer asks vs our preferred):
- Cust: "No liability cap for data breaches" --> Our: "Cap applies except for gross negligence/willful misconduct; for breaches limited to direct damages and capped at fees paid/1M."
- Cust: "We need model training prohibition" --> Our: "Agree to not use customer-provided data for model training or improvement for hosted customers who opt in/out; add admin console flag + audit logs. For public hosted route we can offer contract addendum."
- Cust: "Remove SLA credits cap" --> Our: "Cap credits to a percentage of monthly fees; no consequential damages."
- Cust: "Unlimited indemnity" --> Our: "Narrow to third-party claims resulting from breach of confidentiality or IP infringement by our service; exclude model outputs unless willful misconduct.

Open questions / escalation needed:
- Export controls / sanctions: need legal ops to confirm restrictions on models/embargoed data for certain regions. (Flag: Russia/Belarus/IR).
- Data subject requests (DSR): for hosted customers, define our support role vs customer obligations. Who responds to DSRs when outputs contain personal data?
- State-law privacy (CCPA/CPRA): add data processing addendum for California customers — legal to draft standard DPA template.
- Insurance: what levels are we comfortable with (E&O/Tech liability)? Ops to confirm current limits.

Practical redline templates / snippets to reuse:
- Liability cap: "Except for liability arising from willful misconduct or gross negligence, each party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the amount of fees paid by Customer to Company under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim, or $1,000,000, whichever is greater."
- Data non-use for training (hosted): "Company shall not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to improve, train, or develop machine learning models without Customer's prior written consent. Company may use aggregated and anonymized telemetry for operational and security purposes."
- Post-termination data deletion: "Within thirty (30) days after termination, Company will delete Customer Data from production systems, subject to backup retention for up to ninety (90) days, and provide reasonable export support upon request."

Workflow / tasks:
- Draft updated DPA that covers model training opt-out and residency options. Owner: Maya Patel. Due: 2026-01-10.
- Confirm SOC2 attestation dates and upload to Confluence. Owner: Jordan Lee.
- Get litigation/liability escalation template from outside counsel — ask for approved cap ranges and carve-outs. Owner: Noah Anderson.
- Add a short FAQ for Sales & Solutions about what we can concede vs must not (e.g., liability, IP assignment, training/non-training).

Notes to self / quick heuristics:
- Enterprise with >$1M ARR: more flexible on SLA and residency but push for reasonable caps and audit limits.
- Early-stage startups: favor standard template (faster sales) — avoid making carve-outs that become precedent.
- For Private/on-prem deals: more leeway on indemnities but require strong operational controls + KMS language.

Links / refs: Confluence contract template, GH PR 98 (proposed DPA changes), JIRA RED-2145 (enterprise procurement request).

Unresolved lines in current redline (customer: Acme AI):
- Customer asks for no-model-training clause for hosted instance — can we add an addendum with additional fees? propose: yes, with 20% uplift + strict audit clause.
- Customer wants 30-day termination for convenience vs our standard 60 — lean to compromise at 45 days if revenue > $250k ARR.

Next steps:
- Review with Legal lead (Maya) this week; finalize standard DPA draft; push to Templates repo; prepare Sales FAQ.

-- E.T.
